messages:
Maya: quick sync — last night's canary showed ~0.6% residency-miss for EU tenants. not a huge number but triggers compliance alerts for a couple customers
Liam: can you paste an example of the miss? request path /generate? tenant=acme_eu ?
Maya: yep sample log: `proxy=edge-eu1 path=/v1/generate tenant=acme_eu routed_region=us-west-2 decision=steer-failed reason=cache-miss`
Sasha: hmm looks like edge hinting failed to apply. are we still using the 3-stage probe (cookie -> header -> fallthrough)?
Maya: yes. suspect gap is the header propagation from our API gateway to the regional proxy. gateway strips unknown headers unless whitelisted.
Liam: that fits. current whitelist only has `x-client-region` for internal clients. we intentionally avoid exposing arbitrary headers to customers.
Raj: ops question — if header is missing, what's intended fallback? fall back to global? to nearest region? per contract some EU tenants must not leave EU.
Ana: contracts require residency for write requests; reads can be grey-area but we treat them as residency-sensitive too for now. fallback to non-EU is unacceptable for those tenants.
Maya: proposal: introduce an internal-only hint `x-rdwy-residency` injected at auth edge after tenant lookup. edge will only expose it to our internal proxies. gateway will whitelist internal-only headers.
Liam: OK but two safety concerns: 1) header spoofing by clients if leaks; 2) misrouting when regional capacity saturated.
Sasha: for (1) enforce header injection at the auth layer and strip on ingress from public interfaces. for (2) add soft-fallback policy that never routes residency-write out of region; instead return 429 with `x-retry-after` or queue on dedicated capacity.
Raj: ops prefers circuit-breaker + async queue for writes. we can surface progress via webhook. returning 429 keeps SLAs predictable.
Ana: UX question — will this break existing customers who expect eventual success? need to notify customers on residency SLA docs.
Maya: timeline idea: short-term patch (1 week) = whitelist header + inject at auth; medium (3 weeks) = add tenancy metadata `residency_tag` to tenant record and enrich tracing; long-term (quarter) = region-steering client hints + probabilistic failover testing.
Liam: on the medium term, storing residency_tag in the tenant record solves enforcement at the proxy without relying on headers. proxies can pull tenant metadata from shard cache. but cache staleness is the usual footgun.
Sasha: we should version the tenant flag and include a TTL; also implement a fast invalidation RPC for emergency change (e.g., legal takedown).
Maya: metrics gap — we currently only emit routed_region and decision tags on request spans, but nothing for "enforcement outcome" vs "intended residency". need a 4xx/5xx split for residency enforcement too.
Raj: add two counters: `residency.enforced.miss` and `residency.blocked.write`. also histogram of failover-latency when queueing.
Ana: agree. ops needs dashboards for customers with residency contracts (filter by tenant tag). include alert when miss_rate > 0.1% over 10m.
Liam: implementation note: proxy changes touch kernel filter for header whitelisting + routing layer. safe rollout: add feature-flagged injection, canary to small tenant cohort, monitor `enforced.miss`
Maya: sample config for the auth injector (draft):
```yaml
auth_injector:
  inject_headers:
    - name: x-rdwy-residency
      source: tenant.metadata.residency_tag
  whitelist_at_gateway: true
  internal_only: true
```
Sasha: also add an end-to-end integration test: simulate tenant with residency_tag=eu, set gateway to drop headers, expect proxy to still route to eu when injector active; when injector off, expect 429 for write.
Raj: ops runbook item: if the eu pool is depleted, do not fallback — instead set tenant to "degraded-pending" and notify SE to provision Dedicated capacity or accept temporary queueing.
Maya: open question: do we want an emergency legal override that can route out-of-region for specific tenants? legal says no unless CPLA signed. keep that out of infra for now.
Ana: communications — I'll draft a small notice for customers with residency contracts describing behavior and expected error codes (429 + `X-Redwood-Residency-Reason`).
Liam: perf note: steering adds a bit of latency at auth (<2ms) and tiny memory for tenant cache. quantization-friendly. ok from infra side.
oncall-bot: NOTE: Canary deploy scheduled to eu-west-1 at 2026-04-02T03:00Z (canary-group: 5 tenants)
deploy-bot: Canary deployment started to eu-west-1 for feature/residency-injector (build b472a)
Maya: thanks — I'll open RFC follow-up with checklist: header-injector PR, tenant-tag migration, proxy routing tests, metrics + dashboards, runbook + customer note. tagging owners: @Liam for proxy, @Sasha for tests, @Raj for runbook, @Ana for comms.
Liam: will pick up proxy PR today.
Sasha: writing tests now, will push by EOD.
Raj: drafting runbook and capacity checklist.
Ana: drafting customer note and support script.
Maya: ok team — short sync tomorrow after canary completes. :thumbsup:
